newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open stronger amid supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open stronger amid supply concerns.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger in moderate trade on Thursday, amid concerns about the shortage of some issues of T-bills and expectations that the Bank of Canada will hold rates steady, dealers said.

"It seems to be a combination of factors, both fundamental and technical that are conspiring to keep the market at these low levels," said Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management Inc.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.13 percent from 3.16 percent at the close of trading on Wednesday.

A shortage of some issues has plagued the money market over the past several sessions, with a major squeeze taking place in the one-year portion of the curve. The situation was so bad that the Bank of Canada on Wednesday reopened the issue to add C$500 million in supply.
Posiewko said T-bill shortages had affected the entire market, with many dealers hesitant to be short of T-bills at any portion of the curve.
Waning concern about the chances of a near-term Bank of Canada rate hike also provided support for the money market, dealers said.
Tame U.S. inflation data and a steady Canadian dollar have contributed to the growing expectations that the central bank will remain on hold.
"The longer the currency sits at these levels (the more) I think that we're not going to hike here," said one T-bill trader with a Canadian bank.

In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.65 percent from 3.67 percent on Wednesday. The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 4.03 percent from 4.06 percent, while the one year cash T-bill jumped to yield 3.90 percent from 4.14 percent.

The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.35 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range. Dealers said the rise in the call loan rate was linked to settlement pressures from the weekly T-bill auction.
